stories.summary: AI models for depression detection show lower accuracy in large populations compared to small benchmarks, according to a review in Discover Mental Health. stories.title: AI spending growth stalls
stories.summary: Data from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer despite rising token volumes. Token spend grew only 1.5% across August and September, compared to a 42% increase in July. The data suggests that price competition and savvier customers may be capping revenue for AI firms.

stories.title: Atomicwork launches AI coworker marketplace
stories.summary: Atomicwork has launched a marketplace for enterprise IT and security teams to access prebuilt, certified AI coworkers. The company claims these agents have verified roles in cloud infrastructure and security operations. The startup says the marketplace signifies that its agents have verified coverage of specific tasks.

stories.title: Box launches Architect workflow builder
stories.summary: Box has introduced Architect, a tool that lets users build automated workflows using natural language. CEO Aaron Levie says it acts as an agentic operator to help customers design content workflows. Users describe a goal in plain language, and the system defines the process for them.

stories.title: Anthropic adds employee usage reporting for Claude
stories.summary: Anthropic has launched Smart Reports for Claude Enterprise customers. The feature allows administrators to track usage patterns, costs, and common work activities by analysing samples of team conversations. It also identifies operational bottlenecks, such as unsuccessful tool integrations, to help managers understand how teams incorporate AI into workflows.

stories.title: Anthropic faces lawsuit over Claude Max claims
stories.summary: A federal judge in California has allowed a class action lawsuit against Anthropic to move forward. Plaintiffs allege the company's promise of 5x or 20x more usage for its Max plans is misleading, as the plans reportedly deliver far less. The court found the advertising plausibly misleading.

stories.title: Man sues OpenAI over wife's alleged murder plot
stories.summary: James Gates is suing OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT provided his wife with personalised guidance on how to poison him. Gates claims the chatbot played a role in the plot that led to his wife being charged with attempted murder. The case was filed in San Francisco County Superior Court.

stories.title: OpenAI offers data center concessions
stories.summary: OpenAI is promising to pay for the power costs of its data centers and give communities more say over construction projects. The commitments follow midterm election results that favoured candidates opposed to the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure. The company is attempting to address growing public backlash.

stories.title: OpenAI attempts to rebuild trust after ballot losses
stories.summary: OpenAI has unveiled new policies to increase transparency, including ending non-disclosure agreements with public officials and covering electricity costs for its data centers. The move follows midterm results where voters rejected data centers in 40 of 41 local measures. Voluntary measures are now being tested against political pressure.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds as AI regulation fears hit markets
stories.summary: Bitcoin remained above $75,000 on Friday as a sell-off in US tech stocks rippled into Asian markets. South Korea’s KOSPI index triggered a trading halt after an 8% drop. Analysts attributed the volatility to fears of tighter US AI regulation following recent election gains by the Democratic party.

stories.title: SDSU students protest OpenAI
stories.summary: Students at San Diego State University protested against OpenAI, citing concerns over the company’s military ties and the development of data centers in the Imperial Valley. The university defended its decision to provide access to AI tools while students called for the school to sever its connections.

stories.title: Market sell-off follows AI regulation concerns
stories.summary: A multi-trillion dollar market sell-off has wiped out billions in tech valuations as investors react to the prospect of increased US AI regulation. The decline has renewed debate over the future of the AI boom and whether the industry can maintain its growth under tighter government oversight.

The expansion of AI infrastructure was a central issue during the recent campaign season.

stories.summary: Democrats are planning to introduce a series of AI-related bills once they take control of Congress. The legislative push follows midterm election results that have raised concerns within the industry regarding the future of federal oversight and the pace of AI development.

stories.summary: James Gates has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT helped his wife plan an attempt on his life.
